summary: New factory CLI is injection-free and dist copies are in sync, but a missing json import crashes checkpoint's bare-JSON envelope path, checkpoint writes state before validating its envelope/declared files, and the new run lock has a check-then-write race that can drop concurrent mutations.

findings.summary: declared_from_envelope's bare-JSON fallback calls json.loads without the module importing json, so `factory checkpoint <stage> --envelope <bare-json-file>` dies with a NameError traceback instead of the intended CLIError refusal.
findings.evidence: commands.py imports os, subprocess, sys, datetime, pathlib and factory_cli submodules but never json; line 475 `block = json.loads(text)` raises NameError (reproduced by executing commands.declared_from_envelope on a bare-JSON file: "NameError: name 'json' is not defined"). The function's docstring documents 'a role output or a bare JSON file (FR-017)' as supported input, and tests cover only fenced-block envelopes (tools/tests/test_commands.py:555-570), so the failure path shipped untested (ENG-1). The NameError is uncaught by the CLIError/StateError handlers in cli.py:288-293, so it exits with a traceback and, because cmd_checkpoint already ran write_run (commands.py:532) before reading the envelope, the state file is left advanced and the worktree commit skipped. All five dist copies are byte-identical to core, so every installed harness carries the defect.
findings.fix: Add `import json` to commands.py; extend the envelope tests to the bare-JSON input, and read/validate the envelope before write_run mutates state.

findings.summary: cmd_checkpoint mutates and writes the run state before validating the envelope and the declared-files existence check, so any refusal after line 532 leaves the stage advanced with the worktree uncommitted.
findings.evidence: Order in cmd_checkpoint: write_run(path, loaded, mutate) at line 532 (advances stage, appends history, migrates relay answers into decisions and clears relay) precedes declared_from_envelope (line 535) and the `missing` declared-files refusal (lines 539-541). A checkpoint that dies there has already consumed the gate transition in state.json while the worktree commit never runs; replaying the checkpoint after fixing the cause double-appends the history entry and re-runs the relay migration. ENG-26 requires accounting for partial failures; ENG-24 requires protecting consequential operations from duplicate effects.
findings.fix: Read and validate the envelope and check declared-file existence before calling write_run; perform the state mutation and commit only after every refusal point has passed.

findings.summary: lock.acquire is a check-then-write sequence without exclusive creation, so two concurrent writers can both believe they hold the run lock and the loser's whole-file state mutation is silently dropped.
findings.evidence: acquire (lock.py:92-104) reads the existing lock with read() and, when none is live, writes its own with _write() (plain os.replace of a per-PID temp file). Two factory processes writing the same run both read 'no lock', both replace the lock file, and both proceed into state.write_state (state.py:383-393), a full-file read-modify-write where the final os.replace wins and the other writer's appended timeline/ledger/verify entry vanishes, including the verify-pass record the review gate reads (checks.py:179-187). FR-005, R4, ENG-23.
findings.fix: Create the lock with O_CREAT|O_EXCL (or an atomic link/rename-from-unique-temp protocol) so acquisition itself is the mutual-exclusion point, retrying or raising LockHeld when the file already exists.
